Test whether inverse-error weighting over full pool beats robust median/trimmed_mean; top-3 models (ETS,THETA,ARIMA) have small but consistent error advantage; unstable rankings suggest weights may overfit but worth testing as different KIND
Robust median on top-7 SMAPE pool: tests whether a smaller diverse subset (spanning both error-correlation groups) outperforms full-pool median under unstable rankings
DBA optimizes blend weights on the 7-model pool4; tests whether optimization beats median's robustness under unstable rankings (tau=-0.138) and high error correlation (0.856)
Per-horizon top-3 weighting on pool4: exploits unstable cross-window rankings by letting different models lead at different steps within the robust narrow pool that already leads
Testing whether mean (lower bias) beats median (more robust) when all 6 pool4 models are close in error and predict divergent slopes on the strong-trend series

Robust central-tendency on the ARIMA-group pool; tests whether trimming 20% of extremes (keeping middle 60%) beats the pure median while still protecting against the strong slope disagreement among models
Robust median on broader 10-model pool (by smape) to capture complementarity from CWT_rf and NaiveMovingAverage while staying robust to unstable rankings (tau=-0.138)
Soft probabilistic weighting on the best pool; different from hard topk_per_horizon and from uniform trimmed_mean; tests whether gentle model differentiation helps on this unstable-ranking series
Mix both error-correlation groups to reduce correlated-error risk; trimmed_mean for robustness given unstable ranking (tau=-0.138)

Robust trimmed mean on 10-model pool (adds CWT_rf group diversity); trim removes worst 20% to protect against correlated-error group dragging, motivated by unstable ranking and 'robust' diagnosis hint

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8555. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.138); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.608.
